title: The Afternoon Brief: Ratcliffe's Moscow trip, primary results, and inflation data land
dek: Overnight developments added new primary results in Oklahoma, Georgia, and Alaska and a fresh inflation reading, while the purpose of CIA Director John Ratcliffe's unannounced Moscow trip remained undisclosed by both governments.
author: GoCheckMyNews
key_fact: The common thread remains disclosure lagging events: an unexplained Moscow trip, an inflation reading that ran hotter than forecast, and primary results that reshuffle several November contests, all reported without the follow-up context that would explain their fuller significance.
bottom_line: The day's throughline is disclosure lagging the news itself: CIA Director John Ratcliffe's Moscow trip remains without an official explanation, primary results in Oklahoma, Georgia, and Alaska reshaped several November contests, and a hotter-than-forecast July PCE inflation reading of 3.7% followed a seven-month low in consumer confidence. The reporting supports these events occurred as described but does not yet explain the Moscow trip's purpose or resolve the Alaska ballot-naming investigation. Checkpoints ahead include any official word on Ratcliffe's meetings, the outcome of the Secret Service and Alaska grand jury investigations, and the Federal Reserve's response to the inflation data.
body: The picture that carried over from this morning has not resolved. CIA Director John Ratcliffe's unannounced trip to Moscow on Tuesday, August 25, remains without an official account of its purpose or participants from either Washington or Moscow, as the desk reported. A U.S. military C-17 transport plane carried him from Riga to Moscow's Vnukovo airport at approximately 07:04 GMT and returned him to Riga before 17:00 GMT the same day, according to flight tracking data cited in the day's reporting. What has changed since the morning is largely the accumulation of other stories around it, not new detail on the trip itself.

Election results moved the day's second thread forward. N'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas, a 31-year-old democratic socialist and member of the Chickasaw Nation, won the Oklahoma Democratic Senate primary runoff over attorney and minister Jim Priest despite being outspent $57,000 to $315,000, and will face Republican Rep. Kevin Hern in November. In Oklahoma's governor's race, Trump-endorsed Mike Mazzei defeated Attorney General Gentner Drummond in the Republican runoff. In Georgia's 13th District, Everton Blair Jr. defeated Marcye Scott in a special election runoff to serve the remainder of Rep. David Scott's term, with a further contest between Democratic state Rep. Jasmine Clark and Republican Jonathan Chavez set for November. In Alaska, NBC News projects incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan, a second candidate registered as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., and Democrat Mary Peltola will all advance to the general election under the state's ranked-choice system, with state and federal prosecutors investigating whether the second Sullivan's candidacy was part of a conspiracy to confuse voters.

On the economic front, the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, held at 3.7% annually in July, matching June and exceeding the 3.6% economists polled by FactSet had forecast, according to CBS News. Core PCE rose to 3.3%, also above the 3.2% forecast. This followed Tuesday's separate report that the Conference Board's consumer confidence index fell to 89.4 in August from 90.2 in July, a seven-month low, with gasoline prices above $4 per gallon and five years of elevated inflation cited as drivers.

Elsewhere, three non-law enforcement Secret Service communications staff, including communications chief Anthony Guglielmi, were placed on administrative leave Tuesday pending an Office of Professional Responsibility investigation into unspecified alleged misconduct. Tuesday's stories also carried the Pennsylvania measles deaths, described by the reporting as the first measles deaths in the state in 35 years and the first measles deaths reported in the United States in 2026; separate reporting noted three measles deaths occurred in 2025, in New Mexico and Texas. Also carrying over: Iran's Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh's statement that Iran should 'expect an attack' in response to expanded U.S. sanctions under Operation Economic Outcast, the Supreme Court's 6-3 decision lifting a lower-court block on Trump's mail-ballot executive order, the death of country music figure Dolly Parton at age 80, and the death in prison of Sean Grayson, convicted in the killing of Sonya Massey.

Why these developments are unfolding as they are is only partly addressed by the reporting. On Ratcliffe's trip, a former British military attache to Moscow told BBC News that a high-ranking, unannounced visit on short notice typically signals something significant, and speculated it could involve escalation management or U.S. detainees, but this is characterized as speculation, not confirmation. On inflation, the reporting attributes the hotter-than-forecast reading to the numbers themselves without further explanation of underlying causes beyond what CBS News reported. On the primary results, the reporting notes Trump's endorsements in the Oklahoma governor's race and the South Carolina Senate runoff, and financial disparities in the Oklahoma Senate primary, as contextual factors without asserting they were determinative.
Desk boards were not available this cycle, so board-sourced figures cannot be checked against the day's story numbers.

The coming days carry several specific checkpoints. On Ratcliffe, watch for any official statement from Washington or Moscow on the visit's purpose, and any related movement on prisoner releases or Ukraine talks. On South Carolina, votes from Tuesday's runoff between Darline Graham and Rep. Ralph Norman remained the subject of same-day reporting without a declared result in these inputs. On Alaska, watch for developments in the federal grand jury investigation into the Daniel J. Sullivan candidacy. On the Secret Service, watch for the outcome of the Office of Professional Responsibility investigation. On inflation, watch for the Federal Reserve's response to the PCE reading and any scheduled remarks addressing it. On measles, the U.S. status as a measles-eliminated nation is set for review by a panel in November.
